Total work is proportional to the number of pixels times the average ray length in samples [S1, unofficial].

The evidence describes a two-pass raycasting technique. In the second pass, a full-screen quad is rendered, implying that work is performed for every pixel in the viewport (proportional to the number of pixels). For each pixel, a loop iterates while `ray_length > 0`, decrementing `ray_length` by `step_length` in each iteration. This means the number of samples (and thus the work) per pixel is proportional to `ray_length / step_length`. Since `step_length` is a constant parameter for the pass, the work per pixel is proportional to the ray length. Therefore, the total work is proportional to the number of pixels times the average ray length.
